items.rawSummary: President Trump declared the blockade lifted, but both Iranian state media and U.S. Defense Secretary Hegseth confirmed it remained in place, while US mine-clearing operations and Iranian-Omani diplomatic discussions continued.
items.analysis: President Trump's declaration that the naval blockade would be lifted was immediately contradicted by Iranian state media, which reported that the blockade remained in force and that US Navy vessels were warning ships to turn back. Hours later, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth publicly confirmed that the blockade was very much still in place, asserting that the United States controls the strait. The United States continued to pressure Iran through Treasury sanctions on front companies facilitating oil exports and through preparations by US Central Command to clear Iranian mines north of the Musandam Peninsula. The Wall Street Journal had detailed extensive UAE airstrikes on Iranian infrastructure, which Saudi officials worried would increase the risk of retaliation against regional energy sites. Meanwhile, Iran's Foreign Ministry and parliamentary spokesman insisted that passage requires coordination with Tehran and that any future management mechanism is solely an Iran-Oman matter, reinforcing the diplomatic deadlock despite Trump's demand for an immediate toll-free reopening.

items.rawSummary: The U.S. navigates unresolved Iran negotiations and Strait of Hormuz tensions while a federal court reverses the Kennedy Center rebranding, Taiwan call plans shift, and fiscal projections reveal a structural revenue gap amid new reports of presidential stock trades and a disclosure fine.
items.analysis: Iran negotiations remain in flux after a two-hour Situation Room meeting ended without a final decision, though the New York Times reported that Trump administration officials believe an agreement is close; sticking points include unfreezing Iranian funds, sanctions relief, and enrichment commitments. President Trump separately demanded the Strait of Hormuz open immediately without tolls or mines, directly opposing Iranian efforts to assert control, as the Pentagon readied operations near the Musandam Peninsula and the Treasury Department disclosed the seizure of roughly $1 billion in Iranian cryptocurrency assets alongside sanctions on five front companies facilitating oil exports to China. The Pentagon denied Iranian claims of downed U.S. aircraft, and the Wall Street Journal reported that Saudi Arabia complained to the U.S. in April about UAE involvement in airstrikes on Iran. Domestically, a federal judge ordered Trump’s name removed from the Kennedy Center and the president said he would work with Congress to transfer the institution back under legislative control. CBS News reported that a planned call with Taiwan’s leader was reversed, though Pete Hegseth later stated Taiwan policy remains unchanged and outlined a $56 billion budget for drone dominance, with the administration also in talks to fund U.S. drone companies. The Congressional Budget Office projected that mandatory outlays will consistently exceed federal tax revenues by 2031, with net interest reaching an all-time high of 5% of GDP by 2040. HuffPost reported that Trump bought up to $50,000 worth of stock in TKO Group Holdings, UFC’s parent company, shortly before heavily promoting a UFC event at the White House, and the Washington Post reported that Trump was fined $200 for failing to disclose stock trades worth tens of millions of dollars within the required 45-day deadline.

items.analysis: President Trump's declaration that the naval blockade would be lifted was immediately contradicted by Iranian state media, which reported that the blockade remained in force and that US Navy vessels were warning ships to turn back. Hours later, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth publicly confirmed that the blockade was very much still in place, asserting that the United States controls the strait. The United States continued to pressure Iran through Treasury sanctions on front companies facilitating oil exports and through preparations by US Central Command to clear Iranian mines north of the Musandam Peninsula. The Wall Street Journal had detailed extensive UAE airstrikes on Iranian infrastructure, which Saudi officials worried would increase the risk of retaliation against regional energy sites. Meanwhile, Iran's Foreign Ministry and parliamentary spokesman insisted that passage requires coordination with Tehran and that any future management mechanism is solely an Iran-Oman matter, reinforcing the diplomatic deadlock despite Trump's demand for an immediate toll-free reopening.

items.title: Eastern Pacific Ocean, International Waters: U.S. Southern Command announces a strike in the Eastern Pacific that killed three alleged narco-terrorists on a vessel.
items.description: U.S. Southern Command announces a strike in the Eastern Pacific that killed three alleged narco-terrorists on a vessel.
items.rawSummary: U.S. Southern Command says a strike on a vessel in the Eastern Pacific killed three people it identified as narco-terrorists.
items.analysis: U.S. Southern Command stated that a Joint Task Force Southern Spear operation struck a vessel in the Eastern Pacific Ocean along known narco-trafficking routes, resulting in the death of three individuals the military described as narco-terrorists. The strike was directed by SOUTHCOM Commander General Francis L. Donovan. Such interdiction missions are part of ongoing U.S. counter-narcotics efforts in the region, though the use of lethal force against non-state actors on the high seas remains a sensitive policy area. The announcement did not specify the vessel's flag state or the precise location, nor did it detail the circumstances of the engagement.

items.description: Accounts indicated that Iran was becoming increasingly stubborn in negotiations and making few nuclear concessions, after earlier expectations that a deal was near.
items.rawSummary: Nuclear deal negotiations between the U.S. and Iran encountered fresh obstacles as Tehran hardened its stance and accounts indicated it was making few concessions, while a fragile ceasefire holds alongside intermittent American strikes, disclosures of secret UAE airstrikes, and internal Iranian leadership friction.
items.analysis: Secretary of State Rubio described the Iran deal as a work in progress and stressed President Trump will not accept a bad agreement, even as U.S. military strikes persist—including new strikes on a site threatening forces and traffic in the Strait of Hormuz—and oil markets whipsawed, with WTI crude initially falling 4% to $92 before rising toward $95 per barrel on strike-driven uncertainty. The Wall Street Journal reported that the UAE secretly carried out dozens of airstrikes against Iran during the war, coordinating with the U.S. and Israel, targeting military and energy sites and continuing until after the ceasefire was announced, intensifying tensions between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh over the regional response. Vice President JD Vance said Iran wants a deal and to reopen the Strait, acknowledged that ceasefires can have messy flare-ups from lower-level communication but maintained the ceasefire is broadly holding, even as CNN reported that Iran used bulldozers to reopen at least 50 tunnel entrances across 18 underground missile sites, restoring access to missiles sealed by earlier U.S.-Israeli strikes. Iranian and U.S. accounts of the nuclear negotiations have diverged sharply; Iranian officials indicated on May 30 they will not accept President Trump’s most recent demands, and accounts subsequently suggested Iran is becoming increasingly stubborn and offering few nuclear concessions, dampening earlier expectations that a deal was near. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent offered a stark characterization of the leadership landscape, stating the U.S. did not pursue regime change but had decapitated the first and second levels of Iran's leadership, leaving third-level officials in charge. Meanwhile, a public rift emerged between President Pezeshkian and the IRGC over internet controls, and internet access gradually returned after an 88-day nationwide blackout.
